description: m5 QED recomputed on single-fragment molecules only, with the single-fragment rate as its stated denominator. Supersedes the whole-SMILES QED in cfm_decode_chemistry_validity.json.
WHY: The panel computed QED on the whole parsed SMILES. RDKit accepts multi-fragment SMILES, so on a fragmented cohort that number scores a bag of fragments rather than a molecule.

correction_magnitude_is_run_dependent.finding: My earlier statement that m5 was 'understated by 39%' was derived from ONE run (cfm_frag_control) and over-generalised. The real pattern is that the contamination scales with the run's own fragmentation rate.

conclusion.low_fragmentation_runs: single_fragment_rate > 0.47 → the whole-SMILES QED is essentially unchanged (−0.2% / +0.1%). No contamination to correct.
conclusion.high_fragmentation_runs: single_fragment_rate ~0.15 → the reported value drops 34-36%. Those runs were flattering the metric by more than half.
conclusion.what_to_quote: qed_single_fragment together with single_fragment_rate. Never qed alone.
conclusion.direction_of_the_fix: the corrected number is WORSE, not better. A metric fix is allowed to make the project look worse; that is the sign it was a fix.

not_the_fix_taken: QED on the largest fragment is also wrong — it reads 0.2718 on cfm_frag_control, HIGHER than both, because taking the biggest piece of a bag of fragments flatters it. Recorded as qed_largest_fragment_all for comparison only. [NOTE 2026-10-31: the 0.2718 figure is from cfm_frag_control, whose CSV is not on disk, so it is not re-verifiable. On the 66-row era-B pool qed_largest_fragment_all is 0.09473 against qed_whole 0.09444 and qed_single_fragment 0.09232 -- the largest-fragment value is indistinguishable from the whole-SMILES value there, because only 2/66 molecules are multi-fragment.]
caution: Every row is a single training run. frag_control (qed_single 0.1246) and frag_assemble (0.1275) differ by less than a seed's worth of variation; do not read a direction into that pair.

reproducibility_2026_10_11.direction_on_the_four_csvs_that_exist: OPPOSITE to the table above. On all four real cohorts the single-fragment QED is HIGHER than the whole-SMILES QED (+3.7% to +9.8%), not 34-36% lower. The sign of the correction is therefore NOT established: it was negative on the two high-fragmentation runs cited (sfr 0.15-0.18) and is positive on every cohort that can actually be re-scored today (sfr 0.45-0.78). [CORRECTION 2026-10-31: 'it is positive on every cohort that can actually be re-scored today' is now FALSE. The cfm_fullcorpus_2026_10_10 pool was re-scored on 2026-10-31 after its CSV was rewritten to 66 rows of FREE GENERATION, and on it the single-fragment QED is LOWER than the whole-SMILES QED: 0.0923 vs 0.0944, i.e. -2.24%. That is the same SIGN as the lost high-fragmentation free-generation rows (-34%..-36%) and the OPPOSITE sign to the three reconstruction cohorts, which are the only cohorts left with a positive sign. The sign of the correction is therefore STILL not established: positive on the three reconstruction cohorts, negative on the one free-generation cohort that exists on disk, and on a 3.03%-fragmented pool the magnitude is 15x smaller than on the ~85%-fragmented runs of the lost table.]
reproducibility_2026_10_11.mechanism: The two effects compete. Taking the whole parsed SMILES mixes fragments into one score; restricting to single-fragment molecules ALSO changes the population, because connected molecules are typically the larger ones and QED penalises small molecules. Which effect dominates depends on the cohort's fragmentation rate, so no single fixed percentage is the correction.
reproducibility_2026_10_11.code_verification: molmetal/scripts/cfm_property_panel.py::build_panel filters on n_frags == 1 per molecule. Verified independently: recomputing the mean of 'qed' over the n_frags==1 subset of per_molecule reproduces aggregate['qed_single_fragment']['mean'] exactly (0.11392229108218548 on wf124_p2_cfm_full, n=21). The definition fix is correct; only the magnitude table was unverifiable.
reproducibility_2026_10_11.sample_size_caution: n = 37-47 per cohort, one training run each, one epoch each. These are small. The +3.7% to +9.8% band is an order-of-magnitude-of-the-effect observation, not a tight interval. [UPDATE 2026-10-31: the re-scored cfm_fullcorpus_2026_10_10 cohort is n=66 (64 single-fragment), still one training run, still one epoch (epoch 10, seed 0).]

recomputed_rows_provenance_correction_20.severity: The four rows in recomputed_2026_10_11_rows are NOT generated molecules. [CORRECTION 2026-10-31: this severity statement now holds for only THREE of the four rows. The cfm_fullcorpus_2026_10_10 row was re-scored after its CSV was rewritten (2026-10-12 03:04) to 66 rows of era-B FREE GENERATION; its replacement row is in pool_re_measurement_2026_10_31. The other three rows are untouched and remain reconstructions.]
recomputed_rows_provenance_correction_20.finding: Their CSVs come from molmetal/scripts/wf_cfm_decode_dump_smiles.py, which loads REAL tmQM geometries and runs only the bond head. It never calls generate_clouds_from_noise, so the ODE is never integrated. Every SMILES in those files is a bond-head RECONSTRUCTION of a real corpus molecule. [CORRECTION 2026-10-31: the finding applies to the three reconstruction pools. The cfm_fullcorpus_2026_10_10 pool was produced by the ERA-B path (wf_cfm_decode_dump_smiles.py calling the trainer's own generate_clouds_from_noise ODE sampler), so for that pool the ODE IS integrated -- it DID call generate_clouds_from_noise.]
recomputed_rows_provenance_correction_20.consequence: The +3.7%..+8.5% QED improvement recorded for these runs is the single-fragment filter doing its job on RECONSTRUCTIONS. It is not evidence about the generator, and it must not be compared against the older table's -34%..-36% rows, which DID come from free generation (gen_validity 0.23-0.38).
recomputed_rows_provenance_correction_20.why_the_sign_flipped: Two effects compete: mixing fragments into a whole-SMILES QED lowers it, but restricting to single fragments also changes the population (connected molecules are larger, and QED penalises small ones). On a reconstruction cohort with high connectivity (single_fragment_rate 0.67-0.78) the second effect wins; on a free-generation cohort that fragments heavily (0.15-0.18) the first wins. [UPDATE 2026-10-31: the free-generation side of this sentence now has ONE on-disk cohort to test it against -- the 66-row era-B pool, single_fragment_rate 0.9697 -- and there the first effect (mixing fragments into a whole-SMILES QED RAISES it) wins by 2.24%. The fragmentation rate, not the pipeline, sets the magnitude.]
recomputed_rows_provenance_correction_20.still_valid: The definition fix itself is correct and verified -- cfm_property_panel.py::build_panel filters n_frags==1 and reports single_fragment_rate as its denominator. The numbers above are real measurements of real molecules; they just are not measurements of the generator. [UPDATE 2026-10-31: still valid for the three reconstruction rows. For cfm_fullcorpus_2026_10_10 the numbers in pool_re_measurement_2026_10_31 ARE measurements of the generator.]
recomputed_rows_provenance_correction_20.do_not_claim: That m5 QED improved, or worsened, for these runs. Free-generation QED is still UNMEASURED and requires a decode path that integrates the ODE. [CORRECTION 2026-10-31: 'Free-generation QED is still UNMEASURED' is now FALSE. Free-generation QED was MEASURED on 2026-10-31 on the 66-row era-B pool: qed_single_fragment 0.0923 (n=64) and qed_whole 0.0944 (n=66). The claim that m5 QED 'improved or worsened' still must not be made from the 37-row row, which is SUPERSEDED.]

internal_diversity.note: IntDiv1 per MOSES (arXiv:1811.12823). A value above 0.88 exceeds the MOSES training-set reference and is usually read as distribution shift / combinatorial randomness rather than genuine novelty (Vendi Score, arXiv:2210.02410). Do not present a high value here as a strength.

panel_output_aggregate.qed_contamination_note: aggregate['qed'] is QED of the WHOLE parsed SMILES and RDKit accepts multi-fragment input, so on a fragmented cohort it scores a bag of fragments. Report 'qed_single_fragment' together with 'single_fragment_rate'; do not quote 'qed' alone.

what_changed_2026_10_31.sign_flip: On the superseded 37-row era-A reconstruction cohort the single-fragment QED was HIGHER (+8.5%). On the 66-row era-B FREE-GENERATION cohort it is LOWER (-2.24%).
what_changed_2026_10_31.mechanism: The whole-SMILES QED is inflated by the 2 multi-fragment molecules (3.03% of the pool): their whole-SMILES QED is 0.3049 and 0.0196 (mean 0.1623) against 0.0923 for the 64 single-fragment molecules. Those 2 molecules ARE the contamination the definition fix removes, and they raise the aggregate.
what_changed_2026_10_31.first_free_generation_qed: This is the FIRST free-generation cohort in this artifact that exists on disk. Free-generation QED is therefore MEASURED as of 2026-10-31, not UNMEASURED: 0.0923 single-fragment (n=64) and 0.0944 whole (n=66).
what_changed_2026_10_31.versus_the_lost_table: The sign agrees with the PROVENANCE-LOST high-fragmentation free-generation rows (-34%..-36%), but the magnitude is ~15x smaller because this pool fragments at 3.03%, not ~85%.
what_changed_2026_10_31.against_the_target: The target is qed >= 0.50 (metrics/by_metric/qed.json). The measured free-generation QED is 0.0923, i.e. 0.408 BELOW the gate. This is a NEGATIVE result against the target; it is not a near-miss.
what_changed_2026_10_31.not_comparable_to_the_reconstruction_row: The 0.0923 must not be compared against the relative changes of the reconstruction cohorts: those are the same definition applied to a different pipeline. FOUR reconstruction rows carry a relative change inside +3.7%..+9.8% (+3.7 cfm_fullcorpus_b64_2026_10_11, +6.4 wf124_p2_cfm_full, +8.5 cfm_fullcorpus_2026_10_10 -- SUPERSEDED, measured on a 37-row era-A pool that no longer exists on disk, +9.8 cfm_objective_terms_2026_10_11), and their absolute single-fragment QED spans 0.11-0.24 (0.1139 wf124_p2_cfm_full, 0.2241 cfm_objective_terms_2026_10_11, 0.236 cfm_fullcorpus_b64_2026_10_11) -- 1.2x-2.6x this cohort's 0.0923, NOT a single 2.4x.
